strengths: The manuscript addresses a relevant NLP problem: measuring graded human informational contribution in AI-assisted writing. It explicitly distinguishes this objective from human effort and legal authorship. :codex-file-citation{path="/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b02/review-experiment-t4zwajcu/call-f7c1ae5599454c93978aab1df2bb7d7a/manuscript.pdf" purpose="source"}

The known-input score is transparent, training-free, and straightforward to compute from conditional and unconditional sequence likelihoods. The equations make the proposed operational measure easy to understand.

The experiments cover four domains with 2,000 source examples each, five generation repetitions, multiple generators, and surrogate scoring models. The consistent broad ordering across generation modes provides useful preliminary evidence. Human comparisons and 2,500 WildChat examples extend evaluation beyond synthetic distributions.

The paper identifies model checkpoints, source datasets, computational resources, and a public code repository. It also acknowledges that an output can arise from different inputs, an important limitation for attribution without access to the generation process.
weaknesses: The central percentage interpretation is insufficiently established, even within the stated informational scope. Equation (5) measures pointwise log-likelihood gain, which can be negative; negative known-input scores also appear in Figure 7. Consequently, it is not generally the nonnegative shared-information component depicted in Figure 1. The paper needs to distinguish this model-relative diagnostic from a calibrated proportion of human-supplied information and explain its range and reference conditioning.

The text-only extension has a substantive justification gap. Equation (9) establishes a lower bound only for prompts satisfying the chosen plausibility threshold; Equation (10) treats that bound as an estimated minimum without establishing tightness or coverage of actual prompts. The figures make this concern concrete: for Llama-3 poems generated from titles, the estimated-minimum median in Figure 8 is approximately 0.55, above the known-input median of approximately 0.33 in Figure 2. Threshold calibration, sensitivity analysis, and per-example coverage checks are needed before interpreting these estimates as necessary human contribution.

The reported 97.4% agreement with human judgments is conditional on selecting pairs whose proposed scores differ by more than 0.1. This metric-dependent selection excludes close cases and cannot establish performance on an independently sampled population. Random or independently stratified comparisons, including comparisons within generation modes, are needed. Pairwise agreement also validates ordering rather than absolute contribution percentages.

The evaluation does not adequately distinguish informational attribution from simpler correlates. Moving from polishing to summaries, titles, and subjects simultaneously changes input length, lexical overlap, and task instructions. No length-ratio, overlap, or likelihood baselines are reported. This is especially consequential for the text-only estimator: writing h = I(y)/N, Equation (10) becomes 1 + log(tau)/h, exactly a monotone transformation of mean token surprisal for fixed tau. Its added value over likelihood-based scoring remains unestablished.

The robustness evidence is limited to two fixed instructions: choosing unusual words and mimicking human writing. These are useful perturbation checks, but they do not establish resistance to adaptive attacks that explicitly optimize the published score. The robustness claims should be restricted accordingly.

Reproducibility cannot be fully assessed from the supplied materials. The referenced supplement containing preprocessing, generation prompts, and annotation instructions is absent from the provided PDF. Annotator counts and agreement, random seeds, chat templates, and whether scoring probabilities incorporate generation temperature are not specified here. The code link is positive, but these details are needed to assess the human study and reproduce the measurements reliably.
